$comment: Audit trail AND display source of truth for clause citations whose state has no ingest adapter yet. These clauses render as honest 'text pending' cards — the app never shows words for them — but the citation itself must be right, because a child sees it and a teacher may follow it. The bundle builder uses the `citation` string here in preference to the one it derives mechanically from the URN, because some citations cannot be derived: New Hampshire articles have no sections, and a superseded constitution needs its year. Each entry records how it was verified and when.

verified.subject: amendment by two successive legislatures, with no popular ratification vote
verified.method: web research against official Delaware code and mirrors; page fetch blocked from the build environment, corroborated across independent search extractions
verified.caveat: Delaware is the only state where the legislature amends the constitution without a vote of the people. Article XVI Section 2 provides a convention route, also legislature-initiated; neither is a citizen initiative.

verified.subject: the citizen initiative power
verified.method: web research against Justia and official mirrors; page fetch blocked, corroborated across independent search extractions

verified.subject: election of Supreme Court justices by the qualified voters
verified.method: web research against the official Texas statutes PDF and Justia; page fetch blocked, corroborated across independent search extractions
verified.caveat: Section 2 elects the Supreme Court specifically. Texas elects its other courts under Sections 4, 6, 7, 15 and 18; Section 7 (district judges) would broaden the support if the option is ever reworded beyond the high court.

verified.citation: New Hampshire Constitution, Part Second, Article 83
verified.subject: the state duty to cherish public schools (Encouragement of Literature)
verified.method: web research against nh.gov, Justia, and the Claremont line of cases; page fetch blocked, corroborated across independent search extractions
verified.caveat: CORRECTED 2026-08-07. This clause was previously attached to the local-funding option, which inverted its meaning. Claremont v. Governor (1997, 2002) holds that Article 83 places the duty to fund an adequate education on the STATE, and that a local property tax raised for that purpose is in substance a state tax. It now sits with the state-funding option alongside Missouri Article IX Section 1(a), which is its doctrinal twin. New Hampshire articles have no sections; the URN carries a sec- component only because the URN grammar requires one.

verified.citation: New Hampshire Constitution, Part Second, Article 100
verified.subject: two-thirds of voters required to ratify a constitutional amendment
verified.method: web research against nh.gov and Justia; page fetch blocked, corroborated across independent search extractions
verified.caveat: Two-thirds is the ratification threshold at the polls. The three-fifths figure sometimes quoted is the separate legislative threshold for proposing. New Hampshire articles have no sections; the URN carries a sec- component only because the grammar requires one.

verified.subject: 60% voter approval required for a constitutional amendment
verified.method: web research against flsenate.gov and mirrors; page fetch blocked, corroborated across independent search extractions
verified.caveat: The 60% rule is the general threshold. Article XI Section 7 requires two-thirds for amendments imposing a new state tax or fee.

verified.citation: Virginia Constitution of 1830, Article III, Section 14 (superseded)
verified.subject: freehold property qualification for voting
verified.method: web research against archival transcriptions of the 1830 Virginia constitution; page fetch blocked, corroborated across independent search extractions
verified.caveat: REPLACES urn:const:us:va:art-02:sec-01, which was WRONG: the modern Article II Section 1 sets universal adult suffrage (citizen, eighteen, resident) and contains no property qualification, so it was being cited as authority for the opposite of what it says. The 1830 constitution is the honest source for a freehold franchise; Virginia was the last state to drop one, in 1851. The URN is undated because the exact effective date was not verified — the vintage is carried in the citation string instead. The clause also restricted the franchise by race and sex, which is why it is flagged historical_harm and never renders raw for the 8-10 band.

verified.subject: authority for school districts to levy local property taxes to maintain their own schools
verified.method: web research against the official Texas Legislature page and Justia; page fetch blocked from the build environment, wording matched across three independent extractions
verified.caveat: Permissive, not mandatory: the legislature MAY authorize the district tax, and district voters must approve it. Texas also carries a state-duty clause at Article VII Section 1, which the Edgewood cases read to require substantially equal access to revenue - hence recapture. Texas is a both/and state, cited here because it is the canonical local-property-tax school finance state and its constitution says so in text.

verified.subject: no state ad valorem tax, which leaves the school property tax base district by district
verified.method: web research against Justia; page fetch blocked, corroborated across independent extractions
verified.caveat: This is the provision that actually entrenches localism: barred from a state property tax, the state cannot fund schools from that base at all. Cited alongside Article VII Section 3(e) because the permissive grant alone would not carry the point.

unverified.$note: All previously-inherited citations have now been verified. Any future ref added without an entry above should be treated as unverified until checked.
